evidence.quote: 根据海外加密记者 @EleanorTerrett  的爆料，SEC 公司金融部在 9 月 28 日更新了关于代币回购的 FAQ。修订后的核心是：
针对代币回购，加了四个字的豁免前提，即“没有中心方（no central party）”才行。
这道界限如果生效，会直接将当前的几十个回购标的分成两拨：
一类是协议机制派（如 $HYPE、$UNI）。它们的回购资金流向无私钥地址或直接销毁，全程由底层参数驱动，没有团队干预。这种真正“无人操盘”的机制，在本次更新中获得了极大的合规安全垫。
另一类是团队主导派（如 $PUMP、$ENA 以及各类新发代币）。只要回购额度还需要实体开会决定，本质上依然是“科技公司在分配利润”。这精准踩中了 SEC 想打击的管理红线。
所以之后在评价一个代币的回购是否具有稳健基本面时，可能还要考虑回购资金从哪来、谁能修改规则，以及是否包含了收益承诺。

NEW: The SEC clarifies that token buyback announcements from issuers of decentralized crypto assets do not constitute a promise of essential managerial efforts under Howey, though the same buyback tied to yield on a non-functional network could. https://t.co/yju4d5WOMU

items.summary: Bitget黑客约2162枚SOL被Chainflip拒收退回，约10分钟后经新中转地址再次存入，这次通过了。慢雾余弦称AML/KYT跟不上自动化洗币速度，赃款最终换成BTC后再做CoinJoin。
items.author: OdailyChina
items.new_information: 被拒约10分钟后换地址重试成功

evidence.quote: 9 月 29 日凌晨，黑客地址先收到约 6262 枚 SOL，随后拆成 2000、2100、2162.5 枚三笔送进 Chainflip。前两笔顺利通过，第三笔被服务商拒收，退回到另一个黑客地址。大约 10 分钟后，这笔约 2162 枚 SOL 经过一个新的中转地址，再次送进 Chainflip，这次过了。
余弦总结的黑客套路是：用自动化脚本把钱大量打散，通过各种跨链桥分流；被拦下就立刻换路径重试，最后统一换成 BTC，再用 CoinJoin 混币。用他的话说，这是一个「不断在演变的洗币工程」。
一个残酷事实：我跟进跟踪了几小时，Chainflip 桥确实在很努力阻拦朝鲜黑客洗币，可惜的是 AML/KYT 落后黑客洗币速度。洗币团伙自动化大量打散资金，通过各类桥跨到不同链，如果被风控或者阻拦退回就会立即尝试下一条洗币路径，最终都将换成 BTC，然后在 BTC 上 CoinJoin 方式接着混淆洗币。

SlowMist founder Cos stated that cross-chain liquidity protocol Chainflip is indeed making significant efforts to block North Korean hacking groups from laundering stolen funds, but unfortunately, AML and KYT solutions are lagging behind the speed of the attackers' laundering operations. The laundering syndicates employ automated tools to split substantial

funds into smaller amounts and bridge them across multiple blockchains; if intercepted, flagged by risk controls, or refunded, they immediately pivot to the next laundering route. Ultimately, these proceeds are converted into Bitcoin and further obfuscated via CoinJoin.

items.event: NEAR SHIELD拦截与保密余额之争
items.new_information: 作者解释拦截发生在公开存取入口，查看密钥机制此次未动用

evidence.quote: Easily. The door is public. The room is private.
Public: the deposit that puts money in, and the withdrawal that takes it out. Both are ordinary transactions on Ethereum, Tron or Bitcoin, visible to you, me, Arkham and every analytics firm alive.
Private: everything between those two events. Your balance, your trades, your routes, your counterparties.

Near SHIELD works at the door. It read a public deposit address, matched it against stolen-funds intelligence half the industry already shares, and declined. Nothing confidential was opened to do that. Being refused at a door tells you nothing about what is inside the room.

There is also a viewing key mechanism and a compliance council that can open one specific account when law enforcement brings evidence. It exists, it is documented, and it is not what stopped this. The money never got past the door.
NEAR Intents is not ZK privacy like ZEC/XMR - it is not built for money laundering etc. and they say explicitly they can work with government agencies on investigations

NEAR Intents is an execution venue. user signs an outcome, solvers (MM...) compete to fill it, contract settles. solvers can just not quote. SHIELD can refuse a flow or halt one mid-execution. That's a market maker not buying stolen bags.

items.summary: Dan Boneh、Benedikt Bünz等提出PRAWNS，可把Winternitz类一次性哈希签名门限化为t-of-n，链上仍是普通单签。P3b7_指出其不适用SLH-DSA，每次签名需可信分发者，大n版本引入格假设。
items.author: P3b7_
items.new_information: 一次性哈希签名门限化方案及其适用范围与信任假设局限

evidence.quote: Awesome progress on threshold signatures for hash-based schemes. Dan Boneh, Benedikt Bünz and al. show how to turn a Winternitz-style one-time key into a (t)-of-(n) setup while still emitting a normal single-signer signature.
The chain never learns (n) or (t). The trick is a context-aware threshold PRF that derives the hash-chain secrets.

However the construction comes with limitation. It covers one-time WOTS and few-time schemes like XMSS and FORS, so it maps to the compact stateful path of SHRINCS. It does not apply to SLH-DSA, hence not to the stateless fallback.

There is no efficient DKG, so shares still need a centralized trusted dealer for each signature. And the large-(n) variant puts a lattice assumption on the signers, the assumption hash-based signatures were chosen to avoid. The verifier stays hash-only, if the lattice breaks, signers can attack each other, not the chain.
1/ You've probably heard of SHRIMPS. But have you heard of PRAWNS? 🦐
After a months-long research effort, @danboneh, @benediktbuenz, Justin, Yavor, and @nazirkamilla are excited to announce a novel thresholdization scheme for one-time hash-based signatures!

items.summary: Solana发射台Parasite把交易对改为SOL→Host→Parasite：寄生币以宿主币支付手续费，部分销毁宿主币，国库所得换成SOL后回购销毁PARASITE，最多支持三层寄生。Yuanshan0626建议重点看是否有热门币愿当Host、有无寄生币跑出来，以及回购规模能否持续；风险在于收入依赖投机，且多层结构会放大风险传导。
items.author: Yuanshan0626
items.new_information: 宿主币计价加回购的机制、观察指标与风险

evidence.quote: Parasite 改成了 SOL → Host → Parasite。发行新币时，可以选择另一枚已有代币作为 Host，也就是宿主。
每次交易 A，都需要以 STONK 支付手续费，其中一部分直接销毁 STONK，一部分给开发者，一部分进入协议国库，另一部分支付给 Meteora。
国库收到宿主币后，再换成 SOL，回购并销毁 $PARASITE 。
Parasite 最多允许三层寄生。
问题也能看出来。Parasite 目前产生的收入，依然高度依赖投机。不是有人必须完成某种现实金融需求，而是大家为了炒新 Meme，不断交易新 Meme。
假设 STONK → A → B，你买 B，不只是在承担 B 的风险。A 的流动性会影响你，STONK 的流动性也会影响你。层数越深，整个交易路径对上游资产的依赖越强。其中任何一层流动性下降、价格暴跌或者深度不足，都会影响下面的资产。
第一，有没有真正有市场的币愿意成为 Host。如果最后只是 $PARASITE 和一堆小 Meme 互相套娃，模式上限很低。如果 STONK 这种已有流量和社区的资产开始主动接受寄生币，意义完全不同。
第二，有没有寄生币能够真正跑出来。如果所有寄生币最后都是几小时生命周期，那它只是给土狗换了一种发行方式。如果能出现真正的大市值寄生币，市场才会认真研究 Host 选择本身。
第三，PARASITE的回购规模能不能持续增长。如果协议每天只能靠短周期投机产生少量手续费，它仍然只是一个平台Meme。如果整个生态形成稳定交易活动，PARASITE 才开始具备长期价值捕获逻辑。

items.summary: Anthropic发布报告称智谱开源模型GLM-5.3漏洞利用能力接近Claude Mythos Preview（V8测试12%对14%），约4400美元改权重即可将拒绝率从95%降至6%；natolambert批评其强化“开源危险”叙事。
items.author: dotey
items.new_information: 开源模型攻击能力接近Mythos，防护易绕过

evidence.quote: Anthropic 今天发布研究报告，称智谱 AI 的开源模型 GLM-5.3 已经能独立写出可用的网络攻击程序，水平接近 Anthropic 只向少数机构开放的 Claude Mythos Preview，而它的安全防护用简单手段就能绕过。
报告用两项测试衡量模型写“漏洞利用代码”的能力，也就是把软件里的安全缺陷变成真正能攻进系统的程序。在针对 Chrome V8 引擎（浏览器里负责执行网页脚本的部分）的 ExploitBench 上，GLM-5.3 成功率 12%，Mythos Preview 是 14%，更早的模型基本为 0。在 Anthropic 自己的二进制漏洞利用测试上，两者分别是 4% 和 6%。
修改权重的门槛也不高。Anthropic 团队用了约 2200 个 GPU 小时、约 4400 美元，就把 GLM-5.3 对有害请求的拒绝率从 95% 降到 6%，通用能力基本不受影响。更小的 GLM-5.3-Flash 只需约 600 个 GPU 小时。
The finding is that it builds working exploits almost as well as Claude Mythos Preview. You know, the model Anthropic kept locked away for safety.
It insinuates that Z ai (Chinese lab, builds GLM series) doesn't really care about safety and is reckless to take their business strategy.

A plausible view is that open model weights and closed model apis (with some safe guards) are both far closer to being easy to mis-use, rather than API models being closer to safe. The trope "Open Dangerous, Closed Safe" may be closer to "Open Unsafe, Closed Unsafe"
I am very confused why Anthropic wrote a blog post advertising for cybersecurity teams to switch to GLM!?!?
